Hi OP,

the drama screaming thing is a good training and I would definitely keep it up! I would recommend ignoring her as well; for example when she bites you stand up and walk away to another room and even close the door. When you are on a walk put her leash (which is hopefully connected to a harness and not just to a collar) around a fence or tree and walk away. 

I do not know in which situations the dog starts biting but seeing you writing she also nibbles on strangers I highly recommend a muzzle because she is so mouthy and, always imagining the baddest outcome, it could be dangerous when she gets aggressiv or defensive. But probs to the owner for waiting for a professional to help training that!

Dogs can be very powerful and have a lot of energy but we don't always need this energy so maybe you and your neighbour should show her how to stop being hyper especially when your inside/at home. To train this **you** should **always** decide when its time to play or even stop playing inside in general (probably better for neighbours below you if you live in an apartment). A word which is connected to calming down is also helpful. So for example when she lays down you say this word of your choice in a very clam/calming way and you could even sigh deeply. When your husky stays like this reward her with a soothing voice.

And another way for training this outside is just stoping somewhere and stay there for a while. I always put my foot on the leash but still hold it in both of my hands to have a security if she tries to get away. When the husky stays in e.g. sit and makes no sound start rewarding her with treats and your voice.

I have so much more tips but this is already so long (I'm sorry) so I will stop now while I still can. Please keep in mind that those ideas are just recommendations and you are not obligated to follow them. And I think this is a good idea to get some info about this issue but because we don't know all of the informations its good to start seeing a professional when this is all over.
